record.paper_title: Open problems for tractability of multivariate integration
record.original_question: For integration in the weighted Sobolev Hilbert space on [0,1]^d with kernel product_{j=1}^d (1 + gamma_j min(x_j,t_j)) and summable positive nonincreasing weights gamma_j, is the strong-tractability exponent p* equal to 1 if and only if sum gamma_j^{1/2} is finite?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 1$ and consider the weighted Sobolev Hilbert space $H_d$ of functions on $[0,1]^d$ defined as the reproducing-kernel Hilbert space with product kernel
$$K_d(x,t)=\prod_{j=1}^{d}\bigl(1+\gamma_j\,\min(x_j,t_j)\bigr),\qquad x,t\in[0,1]^d,$$
where $(\gamma_j)_{j\ge 1}$ is a fixed nonincreasing sequence of positive real numbers with $\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\gamma_j<\infty$. For the multivariate integration problem $\mathrm{INT}_d(f)=\int_{[0,1]^d}f(x)\,dx$, let $n(\varepsilon,d)$ be the minimal number of function evaluations needed by any (deterministic, linear) algorithm to achieve worst-case error at most $\varepsilon$ relative to the initial error, over the unit ball of $H_d$. The integration problem is called strongly tractable if there exist constants $C,p>0$ such that
$$n(\varepsilon,d)\le C\,\varepsilon^{-p}\qquad\text{for all }d\ge 1,\ \varepsilon\in(0,1),$$
and the strong-tractability exponent is $p^*=\inf\{p>0:\text{such a bound holds}\}$. It is known that under the standing assumption $\sum_j\gamma_j<\infty$ one has $p^*\in[1,2]$.

Question: Is it true that $p^*=1$ if and only if $\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\gamma_j^{1/2}<\infty$?
artifact.status_search_result: Available sources confirm that Sloan and Woźniakowski's framework only pins $p^*$ to the interval $[1,2]$ under $\sum\gamma_j<\infty$, and that the optimal value $p^*=1$ has been achieved constructively under stronger assumptions (such as $\sum\gamma_j^{1/2}<\infty$), but a full "if and only if" characterization of $p^*=1$ in terms of $\sum\gamma_j^{1/2}<\infty$ does not appear to have been established in the literature. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On strong tractability of weighted multivariate integration
status_evidence.snippet: Constructive proof that the epsilon-exponent of strong tractability equals 1 under a stronger condition than Sloan–Woźniakowski.
status_evidence.claim: The optimal exponent p*=1 has been obtained constructively under a strengthened weight condition, but without a matching necessity proof.

status_evidence.title: Open problems for tractability of multivariate integration
status_evidence.snippet: Lists determining the exact value of p* in the weighted Sobolev setting as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The precise characterization of p*=1 is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Tractability of Multivariate Problems, Volume I
status_evidence.snippet: For weighted Sobolev integration, p* is shown to lie in [1,2] when sum of weights is finite; sharp value not determined.
status_evidence.claim: Only the bounds 1 ≤ p* ≤ 2 are known in general.
